task.title: Narrow ForeignTipsOnly to the failures origin actually controls
task.description:
internal/gitstore/sync.go:529-540. state.ForeignTipsOnly = true is set at :535 inside the "if invalidTracking > 0" branch, which returns before the "if invalidReconciled > 0" check at :538. When both counters are nonzero, Sync (:305) proceeds to publishFetched even though a local replay failed. That contradicts the field comment at :60-65 ("A local canonical ref or a failed replay is this clone's own problem and still stops it") and the PR #35 description ("A corrupt local canonical ref or a failed replay still stops publication").

Scenario: origin holds one well-named foreign tip (a code commit pushed to refs/workbook/tasks/WB-...) and this clone also has a divergent task whose replay fails. invalidTracking=1, invalidReconciled=1; fetch returns the tracking error with ForeignTipsOnly=true; publication runs anyway. Not data-destroying, since the push is non-force and a diverged tip is rejected, but it is an undocumented behavior change with no test.

Separately, invalidTracking is also incremented at :423 for "tracking and canonical tips use different history generations", which is a local-versus-remote disagreement rather than something origin alone controls, so the flag name overstates its precondition there too.

Fix direction: set the flag only for the tip.Err != nil tracking case (:405) and only when no other class of failure occurred, or rename it and correct the comment. Either way add a test covering a foreign tip plus a failed local replay.

Deferred from PR #35 (WB-01KZBT4D40T8493847N5HWMGCH) as a minor review finding: the branch's stated goal, that one ref anyone can push does not stop this clone from publishing, holds in the single-cause case that the ticket describes; this is the multi-cause edge.
